title: Grateful Dead Live at Radio Luxembourg on 1972-05-16
source: SBD > MR@7.5ips > Reel@7.5ips > DAT > Cass > DAT (DAT-Heads Tree) > PC > SHN

ai_review.summary: Tight, high‑energy Europe ’72 show with crisp broadcast mix; standout Other One, Playin', China Cat/Rider and superb Garcia leads.
ai_review.review: Fans rave about the compact, radio‑friendly set that still packs plenty of fire – tight performances of The Other One, Playin' in the Band, China Cat > Rider, Truckin' and sing‑along moments like Sing Me Back Home. The FM broadcast source is generally praised as clear and lively, though a few note low organ levels and occasional EQ quirks.

ai_rating.rationale: Average user rating ~4.1 with many 4‑5 star reviews; consistent praise for both performance and sound quality, only minor technical complaints.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Generally crisp and clear FM broadcast mix; some listeners mention mediocre mids, low Pigpen organ level, and a desire for brighter highs, but overall the separation and liveliness are praised.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Short, broadcast‑driven sets that stay tight and to the point; excellent transitions (notably China Cat into Rider) and a fast‑paced overall feel.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia wails on wah‑wah during Playin', delivers soaring leads throughout The Other One intro, and fires intense solos on Truckin' and China Cat.
band_member_comments.Phil: Phil’s bass is powerful with explosive bursts in The Other One; his tone receives high praise across reviews.
band_member_comments.Bob: Weir’s vocals are clear and strong; his lead guitar shines especially on China Cat/Rider, and his voice is noted as being in great shape.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith’s piano cuts through brilliantly, though Pigpen’s organ is mixed too low for many listeners.
band_member_comments.Drums: The drums are described as tight and lively, providing a solid backbone throughout the performance.
